# Getting started

Conjunction Map Framework (CMF) is a single world map that map mods can share. CMF ships the map; other mods tell CMF what they want changed, and CMF decides and draws it. That way several map mods can be installed at once without each shipping its own copy of the map.

An **icon pack** is the simplest kind of CMF mod. It changes how existing map pins look on the full-screen world map: their icon, their legend icon and their colour. It does not add or move pins; from API version 3 any CMF mod can also hide pins, and from API version 4 resize pins and change their labels ([section 5](Writing-Your-Script.md#5-write-your-script)). You do not edit any map file and you do not need Script Merger, FFDec, REDkit or WolvenKit.

This guide is for someone who has made a Witcher 3 mod before but has never seen CMF. It documents API version 19 (`CMFGetVersion()` returns `19`), independently of release numbering. The map applies the registered styles and dispatches the hooks described here. Source and offline package checks are separate from engine compilation, actual loading and gameplay acceptance; features without game-launch evidence say so. [Section 12](Porting-a-Map-Mod.md#12-teaching-examples-moving-a-map-mod-onto-cmf) shows how existing map mods move onto CMF. A finished example is in [`examples/modCMFExampleIconPack`](../../examples/modCMFExampleIconPack/).

## 1. What you need

- Conjunction Map Framework version 1 or later, installed in the game.
- Python 3 to run the CMF pack tool, `tools/cmf_pack.py` from the CMF repository (with its neighbours `cmf_animation.py`, `cmf_cooked_codec.py`, `cmf_cooked_cache.py`, `cmf_texture_cache.py`, `cmf_pin_types.py` and `cmf_pin_types.json`). It needs nothing beyond the standard library.
- Your icons as PNG files ([section 4](Getting-Started.md#4-make-your-art)).

## 2. Quick start

Your pack is a source folder with this layout. The pack tool turns it into the folder players install.

```
modAcmeIcons/                                  the folder name is the pack name and provider id
  art/innkeeper.png                            one PNG per image (a tint-only pack needs none)
  content/scripts/local/modacmeicons_cmf.ws    your start-up script
  README.txt                                   for players
```

Only these belong in it, plus the optional settings files of [section 9](Shipping-Your-Mod.md#9-ship-it). Keep working files (layered art such as `.psd` or `.xcf`, scripts that draw your art) outside the pack folder: the tool refuses unknown files, and ignores anything in `art/` that is not a `.png`.

Commands below say `python`; use `python3` where that is the name of Python 3.

1. Copy `examples/modCMFExampleIconPack` to a new folder and rename it, for example `modAcmeIcons` ([section 3](Getting-Started.md#3-name-your-pack-folder)).
2. Put your PNGs in `art/` and delete the example's.
3. Run `python tools/cmf_pack.py skeleton path/to/modAcmeIcons` and paste what it prints into `content/scripts/local/modacmeicons_cmf.ws` ([section 5](Writing-Your-Script.md#5-write-your-script)). Delete the example's script.
4. Edit `README.txt` from [`pack-readme-template.txt`](../authors/pack-readme-template.txt).
5. Run `python tools/cmf_pack.py build path/to/modAcmeIcons --out path/to/new-folder`, fix anything it reports, and copy the `Mods` folder it writes into the game folder ([section 7](Check-and-Build.md)).

## 3. Name your pack folder

Pick a folder name like `modAcmeIcons`.

- It starts with `mod` and uses only letters, digits and `_`.
- It does **not** start with `mod0000_` or `mod0001_`. Those are reserved for CMF and for Script Merger's output. Avoid `modCMF` too, which CMF uses for its own example and test packs, so players do not mistake yours for part of CMF.
- Your **provider id**, the first argument of every CMF call, is this folder name exactly, with the same capitals.
- **The folder name decides conflicts.** When two packs change the same thing on the same pin type, the pack whose folder name sorts first wins, the way the game picks between two mods that ship the same file. Pick a plain name for your pack; do not choose it to sort early. The player decides the order: in CMF's in-game menu (the Mod order and the rows of each feature) or with `CMFProviderOrder1` to `8` in the settings file ([section 11](For-Players.md)). Capital letters do not affect the order.

## 4. Make your art

One image per pin type you change. The map draws the selected pin and the legend row from the same image, so you do not need selected, highlighted or legend-sized versions.

| Rule | Why | Pack tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Square PNG, a multiple of 4 pixels, from 32 to 128. **96 x 96 is recommended.** | Images are stored as BC3 blocks of 4 x 4 pixels. 96 px covers the selected pin at 4K (about 92 px on screen) without upscaling; larger only adds shimmer. 64 x 64 is proven in game too. | refuses other sizes; notes sizes other than 96 |
| File name lower-case letters, digits and `_`, ending in `.png`, for example `innkeeper.png`. | The file name becomes the image's key, and keys are lower case. | refuses other names |
| Transparent background, straight (not premultiplied) alpha. | What the encoder expects. | |
| Keep the outer 4 pixels fully transparent. | Stops block edges and smoothing from bleeding. | warns |
| Centre the art on the canvas. | The canvas centre lands on the pin's map point. | |
| Use a strong silhouette or a dark outline, and flat colours. | The map behind a pin ranges from sea to parchment. CMF's encoder fits each 4 x 4 block between two colours, so gradients and painted detail shift colour; flat shapes and outlines survive. Thin 1-pixel lines shimmer when the image is drawn at a third of its size. | warns when compression changes colours noticeably |
| If you want other packs' tints to colour your art, paint the parts that should take the tint white or light. | A tint multiplies the art's colours (gold art tinted magenta turns red). | |

**How big it is drawn.** CMF fits your image into the box of the stock glyph it replaces and centres it there, so it comes out the size the original icon was. Some stock glyphs differ a little between states (a full notice board is slightly larger than an empty one), and your image follows them.

**States are separate types.** A completed place is its own type (`MonsterNestDisabled`), and an empty notice board (`NoticeBoard`) is a different type from a full one (`NoticeBoardFull`). Give each state you want to change its own registration (icon or tint); it can reuse the same image. Players usually expect a completed place to keep a look related to the open one. Level variants (`MonsterNest_1` to `_3`) are the exception: API version 1 keys them on the base name, so one `MonsterNest` icon or tint covers every level.

**You rarely need a legend image.** `CMFRegisterIcon` sets the legend row too. Register a separate legend image only when the legend should look different from the pins; the example does it for innkeepers only to show the call.

### Painted art and BC3

Keep your source pictures as RGBA8 PNG; the pack tool reads them that way. When you build, it stores each one as BC3 and nothing else; there is no other output format to choose. BC3 cuts the picture into 4 x 4 squares and fits each square between two colours, so it keeps flat colour and outlines and bends gradients, soft shadows and fine painted detail. The loss happens once, at build.

| Art | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Flat fills, hard outlines, simple shapes | Looks the same |
| Soft edges on a dark outline | Looks nearly the same |
| Gradients, airbrush, many hues in one small area | Steps or colour drift inside a square |
| Painted detail finer than 4 pixels | Blurs into the neighbouring colour |
| Small animated frames of painted art | Each frame drifts a little differently, which can shimmer |

**How to check.** Build, open the map at the size your pin is drawn, and compare with your source. The pack tool's warning is a floor, not a verdict: it speaks only when more than 5 percent of the visible pixels move by more than 40 in a colour channel, so a painted icon can change less than that and still look flatter. If it looks worse, simplify the art (fewer hues in each 4 x 4 square, a stronger outline); a bigger file does not help, and the tool offers no lossless route.

**Size.** BC3 uses 16 bytes for each 4 x 4 block, 1 byte a pixel; RGBA8 uses 4. The cache file is also zlib-packed, so real files are smaller than these raw figures.

| Picture | RGBA8 | BC3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One 96 x 96 | 36,864 bytes | 9,216 bytes |
| 48 frames of 96 x 96 | 1,769,472 bytes (1.69 MiB) | 442,368 bytes (432 KiB) |

BC3 saves file size, not the animation memory limit: `CMFAnimationMemory` (32, 64 or 128 MB) counts decoded pictures at 4 bytes a pixel, whatever the file format, so a 96 x 96 picture costs 36,864 bytes of it either way.

**Masks.** CMF has no mask for a picture. To keep a part still while another part moves (an anvil under a hammer), put the still part alone in the under picture (property 46) and the moving part in the main frames (property 45), both on canvases of the same size with the other part's area transparent. A stage's `offset` is a start offset in frames, not a pixel shift, so there is no per-layer offset or crop today; that is an idea for a later version, not a promise.
